messages:
Alyssa: Heads-up — FerroHealth POC needs strict EU-only data residency for both model inference and logs. They explicitly asked for BYOK (customer-managed KMS/HSM) + list of EU sub-processors and a routing policy that prefers eu-central and eu-west. Want the pricing delta/impact for Dedicated vs Hosted and whether we can guarantee no egress outside EU. Can we sync ops/legal and give an answer by EOD?

Priya (SE): Quick answers: we can pin tenants to dedicated pools in eu-central-1 or eu-west-1 for Dedicated and Redwood Private supports BYOK via KMS integrations (HSM option is add-on). Hosted API defaults to regional routing but not strict residency guarantees unless you use tenant pinning + network controls — so pricing & contract changes apply.

Mike (Sales): Important for deal — need a clear callout: 1) extra monthly fee for BYOK/HSM? 2) committed capacity price vs on-demand? 3) any SLA differences if we enable strict pinning? Can we put numbers in a short table?

Ryan (Ops): Ops notes: we cannot certify 3rd-party sub-processors in the customer's internal list on short notice. Current EU sub-processors are listed in the public matrix (link: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors). Tenant pinning + VPC peering (for Private) prevents egress to other regions; for Hosted we can configure routing preference but fallback behavior may hit non-EU region during regional outages unless you accept a reduced SLA.

sec-bot: Security checklist (auto): customerBYOK=true requires: signed DPA addendum, key escrow policy, KMS connection test, HSM certs if requested. Also trigger DPIA for health data (PHI-ish). Attestation docs: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/eu-byo-kms-attestation

Priya (SE): For routing policy — here's a minimal example we use internally to lock tenant to EU regions with strict failover to a single standby region (no world-wide fallthrough):

```yaml
routing_policy:
  mode: strict_pin
  primary_regions:
    - eu-central-1
    - eu-west-1
  standby_region: eu-central-1-failover
  allow_fallback_outside_eu: false
  kms_key: customer:kms-key-id
```

Priya (SE): Pricing callouts (ballpark until finance gives SKUs): BYOK integration + HSM cert + validation run = one-time professional services (approx $12k–25k) + monthly BYOK handling fee (~$2k/month). Dedicated reserved capacity delta depends on commit size — typical uplift vs hosted on-demand ~30–45% for predictable latency/cost; we can produce exact quote if they commit to X GPUs or QPS.

Mike (Sales): That PS range helps. Can we get a precise SKU-based quote by EOD? Customer wants to submit to procurement tomorrow.

Ryan (Ops): I'll validate operational constraints by EOD: 1) confirm sub-processor list snapshot for EU-only, 2) confirm whether we can add a short-term regional-only failover (no global fallback), 3) estimate lead time for HSM certing if they require on-prem style key separation.

Alyssa: Thanks. Action items: Priya — build the quote (BYOK PS + monthly + dedicated commit examples) and paste here. Ryan — snapshot sub-processors + ops plan. sec-bot — flag which compliance docs are required (DPA/DPIA). I'll request a 30-min call with FerroHealth at 15:00 CET.

Priya (SE): On it — I'll post draft quote + link to a templated DPA clause by 16:30 CET. :thumbsup:

Mike (Sales): I'll lock the 15:00 CET slot and invite legal if needed.

sec-bot: Compliance doc list queued to this thread: [DPA, DPIA, Subprocessor List, BYOK Integration Guide, SOC2 + ISO snapshots].

Ryan (Ops): Snapshot posted: https://redwood.example.com/internal/snapshots/subprocessors/eu-1772468101.csv — includes eu-hosted infra providers + ingress/egress controls. ETA for HSM certing estimate: 10 business days (unless they accept cloud-HSM config which is 3 days).

Alyssa: Perfect. Will follow up after the call.
